chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan Al-Zayyat Al-Basri, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and I had a companion with me, and behold, he was in a room with padded walls, and upon him was a pink sheet, and he had trimmed his beard and applied kohl. So we asked him about some matters. When we arose, he said to me, 'O Hassan!' I said, 'At your service.' He said, 'When it is tomorrow, come to me, you and your companion.' So I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' When it was the next day, I entered upon him, and behold, he was in a room in which there was nothing except a mat, and upon him was a coarse shirt. Then he turned to my companion and said, 'O brother of the people of Basra! You came to me yesterday and I was in the wife's chamber, and yesterday was her day, and the room was her room, and the chattels were her chattels. So she adorned herself for me on the condition that I would adorn myself for her just as she adorned herself for me, so do not let anything enter your heart.' My companion said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! By Allah, something had entered my heart, but as for now, by Allah, Allah has removed what was (in my heart), and I know that the truth is in what you said.'

key_terms.يَوْمَهَا: her day (her turn to be with the husband)

ai.seo_question: What is the lesson regarding marital etiquette and humility in this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s pedagogical use of *takhfif* (humility) and *tazyin* (adornment) to teach spiritual balance, specifically addressing the companion’s subtle jealousy or feeling of exclusion. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Prophet’s household modeling healthy marital dynamics, where mutual beautification is a form of spiritual and social courtesy rather than vanity. The narrative serves as a practical lesson in purifying the heart from *hasad* (envy) through understanding the context of the Imam’s actions.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Zayyat Al Basry who said,

‘I and a companion of mine went to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> was is a recently refurbished room, and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a pink sheet, and had trimmed his<sup>asws</sup> beard and applied kohl. So we asked him<sup>asws</sup> certain questions. So when we arose, he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Hassan!’ I said, ‘At your<sup>asws</sup> service!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it is the morning, so come to me, you and your companion’. So I said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. 
So when it was the morning, we went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> was in a room in which there was nothing except for a mat and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a coarse shirt. Then he<sup>asws</sup> faced towards my companions, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O brother of the people of Al-Basra! You came over to me<sup>asws</sup> yesterday and I<sup>asws</sup> was in the wife’s chamber, and yesterday was her day, and the room was her room, and the chattels were her chattels. So she adorned for me<sup>asws</sup> upon (the condition) that I<sup>asws</sup> would adorn for her just as she had adorned for me<sup>asws</sup>, therefore do not let anything enter your heart’. So my companion said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, there had entered something into my heart, so as for now, so by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Removed what was (in my heart), and I know that the truth is in what you<sup>asws</sup> say’.
en.sarwar: 13. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from al-Hassan al-Zayyat al-Basriy who has said the following:

“My friend and I once visited abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when he (the Imam) was in a well- furnished home. He had a flowery sheet on him, his beard was trimmed and kohl (metallic color eye powder) was applied to his eyes. We asked him (the Imam) certain questions and when we were to leave, he (the Imam) said to me, ‘O Hassan,’ and I replied, ‘Yes, here I am, to obey your command.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Tomorrow come to me with your friend.’ I replied, ‘Yes, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.’ The next day we went to meet him (the Imam) and he (the Imam) was in a house with no furnishing except a mat and was wearing a rough-textured shirt. He (the Imam) turned to my friend and said, ‘O brother from al-Basrah, yesterday you came to me when I was in the house of the woman. Yesterday was her day, the house is her house, and the furnishing is her furnishing. She had dressed up for me on condition that I dress up for her as she had dressed up for me. So do not think anything.’ My friend said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, by Allah there was something in my heart but now by Allah, Allah has removed what was in my heart. The truth is in what you just said.’”
